finding.summary: orjson does not limit recursion for deeply nested JSON documents

verdict.reasoning: This specific advisory (GHSA-pwr2-4v36-6qpr / CVE-2024-27454) concerns unbounded recursion in orjson.loads, not orjson.dumps. Static analysis found orjson imported in only two files, both calling orjson.dumps for serializing pagination responses, and zero production call sites of orjson.loads anywhere in the 322 scanned first-party files. The other JSON parsing seen in the codebase (json_provider.py, seeders.py) uses the stdlib `json.loads`, not orjson, so it is unrelated to this advisory. Since the vulnerable symbol orjson.loads is never invoked by the application, there is no path for an attacker-supplied deeply-nested JSON document to reach the vulnerable recursive parser via this app's code. A separate, different CVE affects orjson.dumps recursion, but that is not the alert being triaged here.

# mealie/pkgs/i18n/json_provider.py (module level)
import json
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path
@dataclass(slots=True)
class JsonProvider:
    translations: dict

# mealie/repos/seed/seeders.py:51-65  IngredientUnitsSeeder.load_data
    def load_data(self, locale: str | None = None) -> Generator[SaveIngredientUnit, None, None]:
        file = self.get_file(locale)

        seen_unit_names = set()
        for unit in json.loads(file.read_text(encoding="utf-8")).values():
            if unit["name"] in seen_unit_names:
                continue

            seen_unit_names.add(unit["name"])
            yield SaveIngredientUnit(
                group_id=self.group_id,
                name=unit["name"],
                description=unit["description"],
                abbreviation=unit["abbreviation"],
            )
